rows.citation: McDougal RA, Morse TM, Carnevale T, et al. (2017). Twenty years of ModelDB and beyond: building essential modeling tools for the future of neuroscience. Journal of Computational Neuroscience, 42(1), 1-10.
rows.model_type: Repository of published computational neuroscience models (mostly NEURON; some NeuroML); not a testing method
rows.controlled_mutations: no - describes model sharing, curation and reuse; no seeded faults or mutants.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - notes users can rerun models with new inputs, but defines no stimulation battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - no feature extraction; ModelView shows model structure and parameters, not response features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no protocol selection of any kind.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - a descriptive resource paper with no evaluation design.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI or automated model editing discussed.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Context and a possible provenance source only. ModelDB supports sharing, auto-launch and viewing; NeuroSem would add behavioural regression testing of edited models, which ModelDB does not provide.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (title, 9 authors, JCNS 42(1):1-10; online 2016-09-15, print issue 2017-02); Europe PMC abstract (PMID 27629590, PMC5279891); NCBI efetch PMC full text scanned for validation/testing/NeuroML passages.
rows.found_via: PubMed E-utilities 'ModelDB[tiab]' and 'reproducibility[tiab] AND ModelDB' | OpenAlex search (anchor); Europe PMC citations (170)

rows.citation: Ji Z, Guo S, Qiao Y, et al. (2024). Automating literature screening and curation with applications to computational neuroscience. Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association, 31(7), 1463-1470.
rows.model_type: LLM and embedding pipeline classifying literature and metadata for ModelDB curation; no neuron models simulated
rows.controlled_mutations: no - screens papers; no neuron models are altered or simulated.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - extracts bibliographic metadata such as cell types and topics, not electrophysiology features.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - tunes LLM prompting (instruction-tuning, chain of thought) for classification; unrelated to stimulation protocols.
rows.heldout_evaluation: unclear - reports classification accuracy on known ModelDB and PubMed sets; split design not checked because full text was not retrieved.
rows.ai_transformations: partial - uses GPT-3.5, GPT-4 and SPECTER2, but for literature curation, not for transforming model code.
rows.software: none (no code repository found in the retrieved abstract or metadata); applied to ModelDB https://modeldb.science
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Uses LLMs on text about models, not on model files. NeuroSem's optional agent study would test whether AI-made model edits keep behaviour, which this work does not address.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (4 authors, JAMIA 31(7):1463-1470, online 2024-05-09; has-preprint 10.1101/2023.12.15.571963); Europe PMC abstract (PMID 38722233, PMC11187430). NCBI efetch returned only front matter, so methods were not read.
rows.found_via: PubMed E-utilities 'ModelDB[tiab]'; Europe PMC '"large language model" AND "computational neuroscience"'

rows.citation: Ma X, Miraucourt LS, Qiu H, et al. (2024). ElecFeX is a user-friendly toolbox for efficient feature extraction from single-cell electrophysiological recordings. Cell Reports Methods, 4(6), 100791.
rows.model_type: Feature-extraction toolbox for experimental patch-clamp recordings; uses a Morris-Lecar model only to test rheobase estimators
rows.controlled_mutations: no - no seeded model faults; simulated Morris-Lecar traces only check its rheobase estimation methods.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - handles recordings under different current-clamp protocols (e.g. step, ramp), but builds no model test battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - customizable measurements such as input resistance, steady-state voltage, rheobase and spike properties, with batch analysis.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no selection or optimization of stimulation protocols.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - demonstrated on diverse recordings to separate neuron subgroups; no held-out testing of model changes.
rows.software: ElecFeX (MATLAB; GPL-3.0 per GitHub API) https://github.com/XinyueMa-neuro/ElecFeX
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: A feature-layer alternative to eFEL (MATLAB, aimed at recordings). NeuroSem would use features only as one step inside mutation-calibrated, multi-protocol regression testing of models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (8 authors, Cell Rep Methods 4(6):100791, 2024-06); Europe PMC abstract and full-text XML (PMID 38848714, PMC11228277); GitHub REST API for repo metadata and license.
rows.found_via: Europe PMC '"current clamp" AND "stimulus protocol" AND model ...'; bioRxiv preprint via WebSearch site:biorxiv.org (eFEL ... BluePyEfe)

rows.citation: Bologna LL, Smiriglia R, Curreri D, et al. (2021). The EBRAINS NeuroFeatureExtract: An Online Resource for the Extraction of Neural Activity Features From Electrophysiological Data. Frontiers in Neuroinformatics, 15, 713899.
rows.model_type: Web service extracting features from experimental electrophysiology traces, formatted for neuron-model optimization
rows.controlled_mutations: no - no model mutants or seeded faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - groups features by stimulus amplitude and exports protocol descriptions, but only for recorded data, not model testing.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - runs eFEL and BluePyEfe on selected traces and reports feature statistics.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - selects no stimulation protocols; output feeds parameter optimization (BluePyOpt), not test design.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - descriptive tool paper; users can run eFEL unit tests, but there is no evaluation design.
rows.software: NeuroFeatureExtract https://hbp-bsp-hhnb.cineca.it/efelg/ ; code https://github.com/cnr-ibf-pa/hbp-bsp-hh-neuron-builder (paper states LGPLv3; GitHub API reports NOASSERTION)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Wraps the same eFEL feature layer NeuroSem plans to reuse, but for experimental data and model fitting. NeuroSem would instead compare feature fingerprints of reference and edited models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (4 authors, Front Neuroinform 15:713899, online 2021-08-26); Europe PMC abstract and full-text XML (PMID 34512300, PMC8427185); GitHub REST API for repo metadata.
rows.found_via: Europe PMC 'eFEL AND electrophysiology' and 'BluePyOpt' | OpenAlex search 'Electrophys Feature Extraction Library eFEL'; WebSearch site:dblp.org electrophysiological feature extraction neuron model validation | OpenAlex search; Europe PMC citations of NeuroML 2010, LEMS, OSB, BluePyOpt

rows.citation: Shuttleworth JG, Lei CL, Whittaker DG, et al. (2023). Empirical Quantification of Predictive Uncertainty Due to Model Discrepancy by Training with an Ensemble of Experimental Designs: An Application to Ion Channel Kinetics. Bulletin of Mathematical Biology, 86(1), 2.
rows.model_type: Cardiac hERG/IKr Markov ion-channel ODE models (Beattie, Wang) under voltage clamp
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - builds two synthetic model-discrepancy cases (data simulated with one model, fitted with another); structural discrepancy, not single-fault mutants.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - uses an ensemble of voltage-clamp protocols (step and ramp designs) for training and validation.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - compares current traces by RMSE, not spike or action-potential features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - protocols chosen for training coverage; ensemble spread estimates uncertainty, and no compact battery is selected.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - checks predictions on validation protocols not used for training; no held-out models or fault families.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shares the idea that agreement under one protocol does not carry to others, but uses it for fitting and uncertainty, not regression testing. NeuroSem targets current-clamp neuron models, single-fault mutants, feature tolerances and greedy battery selection.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (7 authors, Bull Math Biol 86(1) article 2; online 2023-11-24, print issue 2024-01; CC BY 4.0); Europe PMC abstract and full-text XML (PMID 37999811, PMC10673765); GitHub REST API for repo license.
rows.found_via: Europe PMC '("model discrimination" OR "model selection") AND ("voltage protocol" OR "stimulus protocol") AND design' | Europe PMC lens search (optimal experimental design / protocol design)

rows.citation: Shuttleworth JG, Lei CL, Windley MJ, et al. (2024). Evaluating the predictive accuracy of ion channel models using data from multiple experimental designs. bioRxiv (preprint). Journal version: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A, 383(2292), 20240211 (2025), doi:10.1098/rsta.2024.0211.
rows.model_type: Cardiac IKr Markov ion-channel ODE models (Beattie, Kemp, Wang, C-O-I) fitted to high-throughput voltage-clamp data
rows.controlled_mutations: no - compares four literature model structures on real data; no seeded single faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - an ensemble of voltage-clamp protocols; models are fitted to each protocol and predict the others.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - uses normalized RMSE on current traces, not interpretable spike or action-potential features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - selects no compact protocol set; all training/validation protocol pairs are cross-validated.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - cross-protocol validation heatmaps across cells (wells); protocols are held out, but not models or fault families.
rows.software: https://github.com/CardiacModelling/multiprotocol_data_fitting (URL from journal-version full text; license unverified, GitHub API rate-limited)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Cross-protocol prediction testing for model selection in cardiac channels. NeuroSem would instead detect behaviour changes after edits to neuron models, using mutants, feature tolerances and held-out models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (6 authors, posted 2024-08-19; is-preprint-of 10.1098/rsta.2024.0211); bioRxiv API (v1, biophysics, cc_by, published DOI); Crossref for the RSTA version (383(2292):20240211, 2025-03-13); Europe PMC abstracts (PPR897809; PMID 40078148, PMC11904619) and RSTA full-text XML.
rows.found_via: WebSearch site:biorxiv.org (ion channel model genealogy comparison ... protocols) | PubMed OED/voltage-clamp query; Europe PMC OED query; abstract via Europe PMC
